front.title: A Hybrid Post-Quantum KEM for the Messaging Layer Security (MLS) Protocol

abstract.t:
This document specifies a hybrid classical/post-quantum Key Encapsulation Mechanism (KEM) for use in the ratchet trees of the Messaging Layer Security (MLS) protocol. Each parent node of the ratchet tree carries both a classical and a post-quantum public key, and a direct path update encapsulates to both. The combiner binds both ciphertexts and both public keys, so that the derived node secret is pseudorandom if at least one of the two KEMs remains IND- CCA secure, including against an adversary that controls the keys and ciphertexts of the broken KEM.
This document also specifies an optional asynchronous mode, in which fresh post-quantum output is produced only on designated rotation commits rather than on every commit. Asynchronous mode trades a bounded delay in post-quantum post-compromise recovery for a reduction in post-quantum bandwidth proportional to the rotation interval. Forward secrecy within the rotation window is retained by a one-way ratchet.
This document is independent of the MLS Combiner draft, which achieves hybrid security by a different mechanism: running a pure post-quantum and a traditional MLS session in parallel and injecting a secret exported from the former into the latter as a pre-shared key.
